from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Load the dataset

# Identify the relevant columns
# Labor force participation rate (modeled ILO estimate)
labor_force_col = [col for col in df.columns if 'Labor force participation rate' in col][0]

# School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)
primary_enrollment_col = [col for col in df.columns if 'School enrollment, primary' in col][0]

# School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)
secondary_enrollment_col = [col for col in df.columns if 'School enrollment, secondary' in col][0]

# Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)
export_growth_col = [col for col in df.columns if 'Exports of goods and services' in col][0]

# Extract the relevant data
labor_force = df[labor_force_col]
primary_enrollment = df[primary_enrollment_col]
secondary_enrollment = df[secondary_enrollment_col]
export_growth = df[export_growth_col]

# Combine the variables into a single DataFrame

    'Labor Force Participation': labor_force,
    'Primary Enrollment': primary_enrollment,
    'Secondary Enrollment': secondary_enrollment,
    'Export Growth': export_growth
})

# Drop rows with missing values
data = data.dropna()

# Prepare the data for regression
X = data[['Labor Force Participation', 'Primary Enrollment', 'Secondary Enrollment']]
y = data['Export Growth']

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the rows corresponding to the variables of interest
labor_force_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'].index[0]
primary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'].index[0]
secondary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'].index[0]
export_growth_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'].index[0]

# Extract the data for these rows
labor_force_data = df.iloc[labor_force_row, 4:]
primary_enrollment_data = df.iloc[primary_enrollment_row, 4:]
secondary_enrollment_data = df.iloc[secondary_enrollment_row, 4:]
export_growth_data = df.iloc[export_growth_row, 4:]

# Combine the data into a single DataFrame
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Labor Force Participation': labor_force_data,
    'Primary Enrollment': primary_enrollment_data,
    'Secondary Enrollment': secondary_enrollment_data,
    'Export Growth': export_growth_data
})

# Drop rows with missing values
data = data.dropna()

# Prepare the data for regression
X = data[['Labor Force Participation', 'Primary Enrollment', 'Secondary Enrollment']]
y = data['Export Growth']

# Create a linear regression model
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
